title: Alan Wake 2
summary: Diegetic, minimal UX for the core systems of a narrative survival-horror game, where the interface lives inside the fiction.

meta.label: Team
meta.value: Game and narrative design, UI and game programmers

meta.label: Scope
meta.value: Maps, menus, case board, inventory, weapon quick-select, photo mode, lore browsers

sections.heading: UI that lives inside the story
body: I supported the game and narrative design teams and worked closely with UI and game programmers. The direction was diegetic and minimal: interfaces should feel like part of the world, not a layer on top of it.

sections.heading: No templates for a diegetic deduction tool
body: The case board lets players physically arrange evidence to piece the plot together. Because it lives inside the fiction, there was no standard pattern to lean on. Layout, connection and reading of evidence all had to be found through iteration.
sections.pull: The case board lives inside the fiction, so almost everything about it had to be discovered by hand.

sections.heading: Prototype and test the case board until it worked like a thinking space
body: I tried many setups and interactions, testing how players laid out, connected and read their evidence, until the board felt like a real space for thinking rather than a menu pretending to be one.

media.caption: Every feature here was built in close collaboration, inside the craft team and across the project.

sections.heading: Maps that read at any scale
body: A forest and a single house need to communicate equally clearly. I designed map navigation and camera controls, and worked through everything the map shows, from item pickups to mission markers.

sections.heading: Inventory where space is the rule
body: Items take up physical space in the inventory, and that one rule drove every interaction: drop bullets on a matching stack and they combine, place a different item and the grid rearranges itself.
I also designed the weapon quick-select, a customizable HUD element where players arrange weapons and tools however they like, and the lore browsers for text, audio and video.

sections.heading: A photo mode for real photographers
body: We set out to build the best photo mode in any game. It's grounded in real photography, with camera terms and values a photographer would recognize, plus tools only a game can offer, like an orbital camera free of any physical lens position.
The goal was twofold: a proper instrument for virtual photographers, and images that would carry the game across social media.

sections.heading: Award-winning photo mode
body: In 2024, Alan Wake 2 won Best Photo Mode at The Virtual Photography Awards and placed second for Photo Mode UX.

results.title: Diegetic case board
results.detail: A core narrative system with no existing pattern to copy.
